channel.title: Open Calls for Artists — Monographica
channel.description: Curated list of open calls for photographers and visual artists. Exhibitions, grants, residencies, and publications worldwide.

item.title: 2026 Small Works Exhibition · Charles H. Taylor Visual Arts Center
item.description: Small-works show at Hampton Arts' Charles H. Taylor Visual Arts Center, open to all Hampton regional and Virginia artists aged 18 and over. The call is open to all media; two-dimensional work must be no larger than 8 x 10 inches including the frame and three-dimensional work no larger than 8 inches on any side, with 2D pieces under 20 square inches and 3D pieces under 5 inches cubed judged separately as Miniatures. Work must be original, made within the past two years and not previously shown at the center, and accepted pieces must arrive dry and ready to hang (no sawtooth hangers). One entry per artist covers up to six artworks for $40, or $35 for current Hampton Arts League members. Awards go to First ($200), Second ($150) and Third ($100) Place plus three Awards of Merit across the two categories, and a new $100 Mighty Miniature award for the strongest miniature as chosen by the judge. Notification is by email the week after the deadline; accepted work is delivered to the center November 10-14 and the exhibition runs December 5, 2026 to January 16, 2027, with an artist reception and awards on Saturday, December 5 from 3 to 5 pm. Because the show runs through the holidays, work that sells may be removed at the time of purchase. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $40 (members $35). Prize: $200 First Prize + Cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Bodies & Faces: Art of Figure and Portrait · Art League of New Britain
item.description: Juried exhibition of figure and portrait work at the Art League of New Britain, on view October 9 to November 1, 2026 with an opening reception on Friday, October 9 from 6 to 8 pm. The league accepts all original media - it runs its own annual photography juried exhibition - and the binding eligibility clause is about how the work was made rather than the medium: "Works must have been started from life or have included a live model in the process", so a portrait or figure photograph shot from a live subject qualifies. Open to artists 18 and over; work must be original, completed in the past three years and not previously exhibited at ALNB, with combined framed width per artwork up to 72 inches. Jurying is hybrid - juror Susan Strauss, a portrait artist of more than thirty years and a professor at Tunxis Community College, selects from unsigned images online for anonymous review, then picks the prize winners in person after drop-off. Four cash awards total $375: $200 first, $100 second, $50 third and a $25 honourable mention. Up to five entries at $25 for the first and $15 for each additional ($15/$10 for ALNB members). Accepted work stays up for the whole run, including anything that sells, and pick-up is November 1-3; labels must be attached and an artist contract signed at drop-off, so the show is in practice for artists who can deliver to New Britain. — Deadline: September 18, 2026. Fee: $25 first entry, $15 additional (members $15/$10). Prize: $375 in cash awards + Exhibition.

item.title: Musa International Award for Female Photographers 2026
item.description: Eighth edition of the Musa Award, run by the Lecco photography school Musa Fotografia and going international for the first time in 2026. It is a portfolio prize: each entrant may submit up to three projects of 8 to 25 images, in colour or black and white, mixed technique or other media, assembled as a PDF with a project statement and biography. The theme is "Reclaiming the Frame" - repossessing the power to decide what is worth framing and narrating - and the organisers are explicit that the subjects need not be women, since the point is to see the whole world through women's eyes; every genre is welcome, from architecture and reportage to abstraction and nature. Open to female photographers over 18, amateur or professional, resident in a published list of European countries that includes the EU member states plus the UK, Ukraine, Switzerland, Norway, the Balkans and the microstates. The winner's package is substantial: twenty fine-art exhibition prints produced and donated by Fotofabbrica, an exhibition at the Colorno Photo Life Festival, a screening at the Biennale di Fotografia Femminile in Mantova, a half-hour portfolio review with its artistic director Alessia Locatelli, an editorial meeting with Grazia Dell'Oro of the publisher EMUSE, a filmed interview with curator Loredana De Pace, and €200 towards expenses; reportage projects also exhibit at the Festival Off della Fotografia Etica, and Italian entrants compete for a further show at the Festival della Fotografia Italiana. Entry is €25 for one project, €45 for two and €65 for three, paid at registration with the PDF emailed at the same time. Winners are announced in December 2026. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: €25 (1 project) / €45 (2) / €65 (3). Prize: Exhibition + €200 expenses + Portfolio review.

item.title: Solstice Magazine Issue 74 - Editorial Submissions
item.description: Submit fashion and editorial photography for publication in Issue 74 of Solstice Magazine, a London-based fashion publication. Submissions close 11:59pm EST on 21 November 2026 and the issue is released at 10pm EST on 21 December 2026. Editorials must be unpublished and exclusive to Solstice - work found published elsewhere is pulled and the contributor blacklisted, and accepted work must stay offline until the issue is out. Fashion submissions need a minimum of five outfit changes (beauty submissions, five hair and make-up looks) with at least three finished, retouched photographs of each outfit, and every garment must carry a real brand credit; stylist's own and model's own credits are rejected, including for vintage and second-hand pieces. Website editorials are open year-round and usually publish within two or three working days. There is no submission fee and no payment for editorials; the magazine does not send complimentary print copies but will supply digital tear sheets on request. — Deadline: November 21, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication.

item.title: Rauschenberg Medical Emergency Grants - Cycle 38 · New York Foundation for the Arts
item.description: One-time grants of up to $5,000 for recent unexpected medical, dental and mental-health emergencies, funded by the Robert Rauschenberg Foundation and administered by NYFA. The eligible Visual Arts category names Photography outright, alongside craft/sculpture, painting and printmaking, and the programme also covers digital/electronic arts, video/film and choreography. Applicants must be 21 or older, reside in the United States, the District of Columbia, a Tribal Nation or a U.S. Territory, show sustained public-facing artistic activity over the past five years, and meet the income cap - adjusted gross income no greater than $80,000 individual or $160,000 joint, averaged over the last two federal tax returns. Applicants cannot be enrolled in a degree-seeking programme, and cannot have received a Rauschenberg Medical or Dancer Emergency Grant in the past five years. Cycle 38 covers emergencies that began on or after February 1, 2026; applications opened August 18 and close at 5:00 PM ET on September 15, with notification on November 9, 2026. Artists whose medical costs are covered by Medicare or Medicaid may instead request up to $5,000 in documented living expenses. Roughly $148,000 is distributed each cycle and demand outstrips it, so applying is not a guarantee of an award. — Deadline: September 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $5,000.

item.title: South Carolina State Parks Artist-in-Residence 2027
item.description: A one-week residency in a South Carolina state park, with the park service providing a cabin, a Carolina camper cabin or a campsite; artists may also stay in their own camper or RV at the assigned park. Applications for the 2027 season are accepted September 1-30, 2026, and the programme is open to South Carolina residents and non-residents alike, with collaborative proposals considered. Photography is well represented among past residents: the 2025 cohort included landscape, infrared and night-sky photographer Paul Atkinson at Givhans Ferry and photographer Michael Gambrell at Cheraw. In return each artist donates one original work representative of the stay within 90 days, to be displayed in park cabins and other facilities. Art forms that manipulate or disturb the park's resources, or that use materials from endangered or threatened species, are excluded, and collecting materials from park property is not permitted. Transportation to and from the assigned park is the artist's responsibility, and residents arrange their own reservation once placed; placement depends on the medium each park wants to display. Applications go through ZAPPlication with four images and a $25 fee, and a panel of state park representatives scores entries, keeping a waiting list for cancellations. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: 1-week residency.

item.title: Lakewood Annual Winter Salon 2026 · Lakewood Cultural Center
item.description: The Lakewood Cultural Center's annual salon, a large-scale group exhibition and art market of small, accessibly priced work, running November 6, 2026 to January 2, 2027 with a reception on November 7 from 6 to 8 pm. Photographs are named among the eligible media alongside original painting, drawing, prints and mixed media; reproductions are not accepted. Work must be two-dimensional and no larger than three feet in any direction including the frame, framed and ready to hang with securely attached wire or a cleat system - nothing suspended from the ceiling or standing on the floor. Everything must be for sale and priced at $500 or less, prices cannot be adjusted after entry, and the City of Lakewood takes a 15% commission; artists sign a loan agreement so work is insured while in the Cultural Center's care, and sold work is collected after December 18. Entry is $30 for up to three works. There is no shipping in either direction - work must be hand-delivered to the Lakewood Cultural Center - so in practice the show is limited to artists who can travel to the Denver area. Laine Godsey, the City of Lakewood's Arts Programming Curator, juries the selection. The organiser's own call description sets the schedule as entries accepted on CaFE until Thursday, October 22, 2026 or until the call is full, notification of acceptance by the end of Friday, October 23, and delivery of accepted work during the week of October 26; note that the CaFE record's structured deadline field and one requirement bullet instead give November 6, which is the exhibition's opening day. — Deadline: October 22, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: MCAD–Jerome Foundation Fellowship for Early Career Artists 2026/27
item.description: Four unrestricted $10,000 fellowships for early-career visual artists living in Minnesota, administered by the Minneapolis College of Art and Design and funded by the Jerome Foundation, which has run this programme since 1981 and has backed more than two hundred artists through it. Photography is named outright in the eligible media, alongside painting, sculpture, drawing, printmaking, sequential and comic art, public and social practice, conceptual, installation, graffiti, textile, ceramics, glass, bead, metal, paper, and digital video or film presented in an exhibition or installation context; the programme is aimed at artists who can present work in a gallery. Each fellow receives the $10,000 in unrestricted funds plus $1,000 in reimbursement-based professional development money, three studio visits from professional critics (a local curator, a catalogue writer and a national curator), an exhibition at the MCAD Gallery in January to March 2028, a catalogue with a critical essay on their work, a place on a public panel, access to MCAD's facilities and library, and half-price Continuing Education tuition. The fellowship period runs 1 December 2026 to 15 March 2028. Eligibility is tight and worth reading before applying: you must be a legal Minnesota resident for at least a year before the deadline and stay in the state for the whole fellowship, and you must have between two and ten years of generative practice outside any degree programme. Artists with significant recognition may be too established even inside that window. Applications go through Submittable and ask for proof of residency, ten work samples in any mix of image, audio, video and PDF, a resume, an artist statement and a fellowship goals statement — the guidelines ask that you not use AI or ChatGPT to write either statement. An independent three-person jury scores every application, shortlists twenty-five to thirty, then ten finalists who get twenty-minute online studio visits on 12 and 13 November. Staff take no part in the selection, and MCAD-affiliated applicants can never be more than half of any cohort. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: $10,000 + Exhibition + Catalogue.

item.title: Artist in Residence 2027 · Glen Arbor Arts Center
item.description: A two-week residency on the edge of the Sleeping Bear Dunes National Lakeshore in northern Michigan, offered several times a year by the Glen Arbor Arts Center to give visiting artists a respite from daily responsibilities and concentrated time to work. Photography is named explicitly among the disciplines considered, along with creative writing, visual art, sculpture, fibre arts, ceramics and music. There is no residency fee — housing and studio space are provided free — and the only cost is a non-refundable $35 application fee. Residents stay in a furnished second-floor walk-up apartment with a bedroom, living room, small bath and galley kitchen a short walk from a grocery and restaurants, and bring their own linens and towels; the apartment is not wheelchair accessible, is smoke-free, allows no pets, and art materials may not be used in it. The studio is a restored tool shed at historic Thoreson Farm inside the national lakeshore, 3.7 miles from the arts centre, a rustic seasonal building with a cement floor, overhead lighting, space heaters and some shared equipment. Each residency is a one-person opportunity — groups and collaborative teams are not considered — and residents commit to the full fourteen days, give a community presentation on the second Thursday of their stay, and may be asked, but not required, to donate one work made during the residency to the centre's permanent collection. A car is effectively necessary: Glen Arbor is walkable but the studio is out at the farm and Traverse City is 26 miles away. This round covers the 2027 season, May to October, though July and early August are generally unavailable because the apartment is in use. Visual artists submit six to eight images plus a resume; applications are reviewed straight after the deadline with notification by mid-March. Anyone selected for a Glen Arbor residency in the past three years is not eligible. — Deadline: November 5, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: 2-week residency.

item.title: Photodarium 2028 · Slanted Publishers
item.description: PHOTODARIUM is a tear-off calendar that reveals a new instant photo every day, each with its own little story: the front of each calendar page carries the photograph, the back a short account of how it came about together with the photographer's name, location and URL. Slanted Publishers in Karlsruhe edits the series with Raban Ruddigkeit, and Seltmann Publishers issues it; Boris Kahl is art director and project manager. Submissions must be original scans of instant photos made with a Polaroid SX-70, a 600 or a new Impossible/Polaroid camera — the editors say plainly that they do not accept fakes. Entrants pick up to five favourite calendar days and upload one photo for each, and three photos by different photographers end up competing for any one day. The back-of-page text is treated as part of the submission and will be printed, so the editors warn that a dummy description gets the whole entry refused. Files should be JPG, RGB, 350 dpi at the original size of 88 x 107 mm including the frame. Entry is free; contributors grant Slanted and Seltmann a non-exclusive right to use the photos for the calendars and their promotion, receive a free copy of the calendar if published and a 50 percent discount on further copies, and no financial compensation is paid. The call for entries opens on 1 September 2026 and closes on 25 September 2026, with production and distribution in 2027. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication (print).

item.title: The Print Continuum · East End Arts Council
item.description: East End Arts Council in Riverhead, New York invites printmakers from across the United States to submit to The Print Continuum, a national juried exhibition celebrating the intersection of printmaking's historical traditions and its expanding contemporary practices. A continuum is a spectrum, the council writes, where distinct points are linked by gradual change rather than clear divisions; printmaking is not divided between old and new but is a medium in which history, innovation and experimentation stay in dialogue. Eligible work includes screen printing, relief printing, woodcut, linocut, intaglio, etching, lithography, monotype, collagraph, gel printing, and mixed-media works incorporating hybrid processes on paper, fabric, sculpture or other substrates. Read the medium clause carefully before applying: photography and 3D printing alone are not eligible, but works incorporating those processes within original printmaking or mixed-media pieces will be considered — so photogravure, photopolymer, screenprints made from photographs and photo-based collage are in scope while a straight photographic print is not. Selections are made by artists Ellen Wiener and Bill Albertini, with the exhibition curated by Mich Miller, Head of Printmaking at East End Arts Council. Applications go through CaFE and ask for an artist statement of up to 500 words on creative intent, process and how printmaking contributes to your vision, three to five images with optional detail or installation views, a website or social media link, and an image list. The cap is three submissions of work, each original and not previously shown at East End Arts Council; the three to five images may include multiple views, details or installation shots of those same pieces. There is no size limitation. Selected work hangs at the council's 11 West Gallery from 24 October to 13 December 2026, with an opening reception on 24 October. Awards are $1,000 for first prize, $500 for second and $250 for third. Council members get early access and a 10 percent discount code on the application fee. Read the terms before entering: accepted work must stay available for the whole run and is sold exclusively through the council, which keeps a 50 percent commission from non-members and 30 percent from members, and selected artists arrange and pay for delivery and return themselves. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $30 (10% off for members). Prize: $1,000 + Exhibition.

item.title: Hayama Artist Residency 2027
item.description: Hayama Artist Residency sends artists to Hayama, a coastal town of 33,000 on Japan's Miura Peninsula facing Sagami Bay, for four weeks from 1 to 30 June 2027. Founded and directed by curator Dexter Wimberly, the residency is fully funded: a roundtrip flight to Narita or Haneda, a private bedroom in shared accommodation at hôtel ami hayama for the month, and $800 USD toward meals and local transport. Artists are not required to make new work — the programme is built around rest, research and reflection, immersion in Japanese culture, and meeting artists, curators and gallery owners in Japan. A key component is a group exhibition during the stay, hosted with KOKI ARTS, a contemporary gallery in Tokyo's Bakurocho art district, whose director works with the residency's curatorial team on selection, consignment, shipping and insurance. Open to any visual artist over 21 working in any medium, based anywhere in the world; photography sits squarely in scope — past residents include Joiri Minaya, whom the residency describes as working in photography, digital media, film, performance, sculpture, textiles and painting, and Asim Waqif, who has worked in sculpture, site-specific public installation, video and photography. Applications are reviewed by the director and a selection committee, which for 2026 comprised Alexander Berggruen, Francesca Bertolotti-Bailey, Hilary Burt of SOCO Gallery, Kimberli Gant of the Brooklyn Museum and the artist Yoshua Okón. Submit up to 10 samples in any combination of JPEG, audio or video, with links accepted on a one-page PDF. The $95 application fee is waived for first-time applicants who apply again the following year. Applicants are notified by 15 December 2026. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $95 (waived for second-time applicants). Prize: Funded residency + $800 stipend + Exhibition.

item.title: Winter Residency 2026–27 · Contact Darkroom
item.description: CONTACT Darkroom is a not-for-profit art centre and photographic darkroom in Totnes, Devon, housed in a repurposed abattoir and specialising in black-and-white and colour hand printing. Its winter residency is resource-based: the organisation's own page describes 24-hour-a-day access to fully equipped colour and black-and-white darkrooms, a dedicated workshop room, workspace and an open gallery, for stays of one week to one month between 1 November 2026 and 31 March 2027, with an ideal Friday start. Facilities include a 20-inch RA4 colour processor, three 5x4 black-and-white enlargers, two 5x4 colour enlargers, a large sink, black-and-white film development and an outside suntrap. The residency is designed for emerging and established photographers working on new or existing projects, testing out processes, or making work that responds to the surrounding landscape — the River Dart running from the Dartmoor moorlands to the Atlantic coast. At the end of a residency artists are invited, but not expected, to share work in a small exhibition, talk or workshop; darkroom inductions, guided walks, excursions and local gallery visits can be arranged on request. Applications are open internationally to artists working across photography, film and lens-based practices, and to those making interdisciplinary work engaging image-making, print and alternative processes. There is no application fee, and no closing date is published: complete the form on the residency page with your preferred dates and an outline of your intentions, and the darkroom will arrange a video call. Applications are considered on a rolling basis for stays inside that November–March window. The residency itself is self-funded at £500 per week for one week, £450 per week for two and £400 per week for three weeks or more; inductions to colour and black-and-white printing are charged separately, and private lodging within walking distance is around £50 per night. — Deadline: Continuous. Fee: Free to apply (£400–£500 per week, self-funded). Prize: Darkroom residency.

item.title: art·i·face · midwest nice art
item.description: art·i·face is a juried open call from midwest nice art, the Sioux Falls artist-run curatorial platform, open to artists internationally who work with materials in a surprising manner. Most utilitarian objects have a specific use; the brief asks how artists transform that purpose, citing Robert Rauschenberg's combines, El Anatsui's bottle-cap wall hangings, Ingrid Calame's paintings traced from forgotten stains on the street, and Rachel Whiteread's unconventional casting sculptures. Artists are asked to consider a secondary use or process within their work — jigs, templates, casts, moulds, scraps, detritus and found objects — used as a way of working, as subject matter, or as a route to abstraction. midwest nice art runs all-media themed shows, and the entry form asks only for the title, medium, size and year of each work; photography runs throughout the gallery's exhibition archive, whose credit lines include archival pigment prints, photographic collage and photographs on paper. The juror is Andrew Nordin, an artist and educator who teaches studio art and art history at Ridgewater College and curates its galleries; he holds BFAs in Painting and Graphic Design from St. Cloud State University and an MFA in Pictorial Arts from San José State University, received a 2017 Minnesota State Arts Board award, and recently completed a residency at Natthagen Art Center in Julussdalen, Norway. Up to three works may be submitted for a $5 exhibition fee, paid via Square once the entry form is completed. Images should be 300 dpi and 1500 px on the longest side. The online exhibition opens 15 December 2026. — Deadline: November 20, 2026. Fee: $5. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: The Interpretation of Dreams · Praxis Photo Arts Center
item.description: Juried exhibition at Praxis Gallery in Minneapolis on dream states and interior worlds. Photography is often seen as a record of what is real, but Praxis frames it as a portal into the imagined, the unconscious and the symbolic — where time folds, logic dissolves, and meaning slips through what is revealed and what is withheld. Submissions may encompass constructed realities, surreal compositions, symbolic gestures, lyrical narratives and emotionally resonant abstractions; the gallery welcomes images that feel like fragments of the subconscious, poetic, uncanny or mythic, and states that all lens-based artwork is welcome. Curated by the Praxis directors rather than a guest juror. Up to 38 photographs are selected for the physical gallery show (17 October – 14 November 2026) and featured on the gallery's online exhibition page. Awards are a Directors' Choice (free entry into two future juried calls of the artist's choice) and five honourable mentions featured in the exhibition, the printed exhibition catalogue and the online gallery. Images shown at Praxis within the past year are ineligible. Praxis members get 10 images for the price of 5, and artists experiencing financial hardship may request a free submission. Selected artists either ship an unframed original print or use the gallery's optional $37 printing service; Praxis provides all matting and framing in its 22 × 22-inch black frames, and retains a 50% commission on any sales. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $35 (5 images) + $5 each additional. Prize: Exhibition + catalog.

item.title: Annual Juried Members Show · Art Center Sarasota
item.description: The Annual Juried Members Show at Art Center Sarasota — a 501(c)(3) art centre on Sarasota Bay with four galleries, in its 2025–26 centennial season — is free from a prescribed theme and welcomes original work in all media, with the call naming painting, drawing, photography, printmaking, mixed media, digital arts, sculpture and video. Every current member who submits is guaranteed inclusion, so the jurying decides the awards rather than the hang: Swiss-born Sarasota muralist Alissa Silvers reviews all required information except the artist's name and the artwork price, and selects the awards in person once the show is installed. Awards are 1st place $500, 2nd $300, 3rd $200, plus two Merit Awards and four Honorable Mentions. Work must be original, completed within the last three years and not previously shown at the centre; editioned prints are eligible where labelled and numbered, which the call spells out as covering photography, and copies or reproductions are not. 2D work is capped at 30 × 30 inches after framing. All work must be for sale, with the artist keeping 60% of the selling price. Membership runs from $25 a year for students and $75 for individuals. The exhibition runs 3 December 2026 – 9 January 2027 with an opening reception on the 3rd; accepted work is received in person on 17–18 November or must arrive by post between 16 and 18 November. — Deadline: October 25, 2026. Fee: $30 (1 work), $40 (2), $45 (3); students $10/$20/$25. Prize: $500 + Exhibition.

item.title: TRANSLUCENT · Manifest Gallery
item.description: An international call from Manifest Gallery in Cincinnati for works that employ, depict, or explore translucency and transparency. The gallery names glass, acrylic, plastic, stacks of layers, gossamer weaves, lenses and filters among the materials, subjects and mechanisms that may pierce, reveal and distort, and frames the show as an exhibit of ideas, images, materials and mechanisms that ask you to see through. Open to everyone internationally and to all traditional and non-traditional genre and media, with no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery door and no restriction on when the work was made. Selection is two-stage: an anonymous multi-member panel of professional and academic advisors juries the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibition curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, and one work from each of the nine exhibition periods in Manifest's 23rd season wins a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by a second-round re-jury of the top-scoring works. Selected work is shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027 and documented in the season annual; artists receive 70% on sales. Entry is $45 for up to three works and $5 for each additional work, with no cap on the number of entries, and the prospectus states this jury fee is the only cost charged by Manifest for participation. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: TAPPED 2026 — 17th Annual · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest Gallery's long-running annual exhibit of works by artists shown side by side with works by their current or former instructors, celebrating the legacy of the academic process in art. Now in its 17th year, TAPPED is not a call for collaborative work: each member of a pair submits their own entry form, fee and images, and names the other on their form, with at least as many works submitted as there are companions named. Media is open to all traditional and non-traditional genre and media, including but not limited to sculpture, photography, painting, drawing and printmaking, and the works by each person need not relate in theme, media or style to the other's. The gallery notes that three-way connections — someone tapping both a former teacher and a current or former student — are especially welcome. An anonymous multi-member panel of professional and academic advisors juries the entries and passes its recommendations to the exhibition curator, who makes the final selections. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, one work from each of the nine exhibition periods in Manifest's 23rd season wins a $1,000 Grand Jury Award, and artists receive 70% on sales. Selected work is shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027. Entry is $45 for up to three works plus $5 for each additional work, with no cap on the number of entries. — Deadline: September 13, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: The Manifest Prize 2026 — 17th Annual · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest Gallery's annual competitive award, in which a several-round blind jury reduces an international field to a single work: the winner receives $10,000 in cash and a four-week solo exhibit of that one work, hung in a gallery of its own alongside juror and artist statements. As many as 18 purposely anonymous professional jurors score the entries. Four runner-up works each receive $250 and are published in the Manifest Exhibition Annual. The prize was doubled from $5,000 to $10,000 in 2025 and is entirely separate from the season's nine $1,000 Grand Jury Awards. Media is open to any and all traditional and non-traditional visual arts genre and media, explicitly including photography, video, sculpture, installation, painting, drawing and printmaking, with no size limit and no stylistic preference — the gallery notes that very small works and room-sized works have both won in past years. The only substantive limits are that work must have been completed within the past five years (2021–2026) and must be available for the exhibition period. The winning work is unveiled on December 10, 2026 at a ticketed preview event and shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027; work need not be for sale, and artists receive 70% if it is. Entry is $45 for up to five works by September 15 and $60 for up to five works from September 16 to the final October 6 deadline, plus $5 for each additional work. — Deadline: October 6, 2026. Fee: $60 (5 images) + $5 each; $45 early to Sep 15. Prize: $10,000 + solo exhibition.

item.title: Focus #7 — The Pursuit of Happiness · Les Mesnographies
item.description: Annual open call for Les Mesnographies, the first free open-air photography festival in the Yvelines, staged in the municipal park at Les Mesnuls west of Paris. For its 7th edition the festival invites series responding to the notion of happiness, quoting Oxford's Department of Psychology — happiness as a positive emotion arising not only from doing or receiving something but from a sense of connection between people or of wellbeing — and asking what happiness is: a goal, a state to be reached, something within us or something built over time. The festival hangs work outdoors in the park for three weeks each year, brings together photographers of different nationalities, and runs alongside a free programme of guided visits, talks, a picnic and an opening concert; past editions have shown photographers from Argentina, China and France, and the festival has been covered by M Le Monde, Fisheye, Télérama, Polka, Beaux Arts, France Culture and Arte. It also runs a hors-les-murs strand placing work in nearby communes with the Parc naturel régional de la Haute Vallée de Chevreuse. Applications are a single PDF of no more than 20 images with the series text and a biography, sent by email — the organisers ask that you do not send WeTransfer links. Because the work is shown outdoors in a park open to all audiences including children, the festival asks applicants to keep that in mind when building a series. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Open-air festival exhibition.

item.title: CANINE · Maine Museum of Photographic Arts
item.description: The Maine Museum of Photographic Arts is gathering work for CANINE, an upcoming exhibition it announces with a single word and a William Wegman print. Submissions go by email rather than through a portal: send six to twelve JPEGs sized to 1500 pixels on the longest edge, a short bio of two or three sentences, an artist statement of three to five sentences about the content of the work, and an image list, with 'CANINE SUBMISSION' in the subject line. The museum asks for conceptual fine art images only. No fee is attached to the call. The exhibition is underwritten by the family of Jamie Salomon (1963-2024), a photographer who took up his father's Rolleiflex at twelve, earned a BFA in photography from the School of Visual Arts in New York and built a career in Maine across architectural, editorial and commercial work; an avid nature enthusiast, his knowledge of the woods, oceans and wildlife ran through his pictures. Established in 2010, MMPA is the only museum in Maine dedicated exclusively to photography, artist-run and directed by Denise Froehlich, exhibiting and collecting photographic work and selling contemporary and secondary-market prints through its gallery. It has moved into a new home at 387 Commercial Street in Portland, open Tuesday to Saturday from 11am to 5pm. Submissions close on Tuesday, December 1, 2026. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Pile Press Literary + Art Journal, Issue 13
item.description: Pile Press is an alternative publishing collective in Portland, Oregon making local and limited-edition print publications, and its bi-annual literary and arts journal is open for Issue 13. The journal carries poetry, art, short fiction, creative nonfiction, photography and comics by women and non-binary creatives, and submissions are open only to US residents identifying as women and/or non-binary. Photographers and artists may send up to three pieces, at 300 DPI or better. Simultaneous submissions are allowed as long as you tell the editors promptly if the work is taken elsewhere; previously published work is not accepted, though the press does not count social media as formal publication. There is no payment on publication, but contributors get a contributor rate on the journal and the reach of a title stocked in several bookshops around Portland. Entry costs $4 through Submittable and the reading period runs from August 15 to September 25, 2026. The press also runs CHUNK, a black-and-white Oregon-centric broadside paper open to Oregon residents of any gender on a rolling basis. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $4. Prize: Publication.

item.title: November Gallery Members Exhibition — Cornucopia · Crossroads Art Center
item.description: Crossroads Art Center runs bi-monthly members-only shows, and November's is Cornucopia, which asks for abundance in whatever form the artist finds it — harvest scenes, fruit and florals, the textures of orchards and fields, still lifes bursting with colour, cultural or mythological readings of the horn of plenty, or purely abstract expressions of overflow and richness. Photography sits in the organiser's own eligible-media list alongside painting, mixed media, collage, fibre, sculpture, ceramics, glass, digital art, woodworking and assemblage. Only original work by the entering artist is accepted; reproductions and giclée prints are refused unless the owner approves them, though work where the print process is itself the art — etching, monoprint, silkscreen, lithograph, or images the artist builds in a program such as Procreate or Photoshop — is allowed. Work already accepted into a juried show at the centre may not be entered into a juried show again. Everything must be for sale, must stay up for the run, and 2-D pieces must be wired rather than hung on sawtooth hangers. The gallery takes 30 per cent of sales and the artist keeps 70. Entry costs $15 per submission with a limit of three, and is open to current CAC gallery members, a $50-a-year status ($40 for resident artists) that is separate from the centre's Artist-in-Residence programme. Entries run October 1 to 18 through ArtCall, artists hear by October 23, work is delivered November 10 to 13, and the show opens on November 20 and runs live and online until January 3, 2027. — Deadline: October 18, 2026. Fee: $15 per work (CAC gallery membership required, $50/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Through a Lens that Protects Nature and Preserves the Future · Hamdan Bin Mohammed Bin Rashid Al Maktoum
item.description: HIPA runs this competition with the Dubai Environment and Climate Change Authority, inviting photographers from around the world to photograph the natural heritage of the United Arab Emirates. There are four categories. Wildlife covers animals, birds, insects and wild plants in their natural habitats; Natural Landscapes covers mountains, deserts, forests, valleys, coastlines and other natural scenery and phenomena; Underwater World covers marine life, coral reefs, aquatic species and underwater landscapes in the UAE's coastal and marine waters; and Nature Reimagined With AI asks entrants to rework an original nature photograph through artificial intelligence, with the result still showing a recognisable connection to the UAE. Every photograph entered in the three photographic categories must have been captured in the UAE. Entry is free and open to individuals aged 18 and over anywhere in the world, one photo per category and four entries at most. Files must be JPEG, at least 5 MB, no less than 2000 pixels on the longest edge and 300 dpi, carrying no signature, border, watermark or logo; phone and drone photographs are allowed. Basic technical editing is acceptable, but compositing, creative retouching and any manipulation used to create illusions or deceptions is prohibited outside the AI category. The prize table pays 15,000 / 10,000 / 5,000 for first, second and third place in each of Wildlife, Natural Landscapes and Underwater World and 10,000 for first place in the AI category; HIPA publishes those figures without naming a currency. Entrants are asked to follow a published environmental photography ethics code: keep a safe distance from wildlife and never chase or frighten it, do not handle, feed or relocate living things or interfere with nests, breeding sites or resting areas, leave plants and rocks where they are, stay on designated trails, obtain any permits required for protected and marine areas, avoid lighting or sound that alters natural behaviour, and fly drones only under the permits and in the areas allowed in Dubai and the UAE. Submissions opened on 21 August 2026 and close at 24:00 UAE time on 2 September. — Deadline: September 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 15,000 cash per category (currency unnamed).

item.title: 2026 Annual Members' Exhibit · Umpqua Valley Arts
item.description: Umpqua Valley Arts gives its galleries over to its own members each autumn, and the 2026 edition is non-juried, has no theme and takes any medium: every active UVA Artist Member may submit one piece and it goes on the wall. Work must have been made within the last five years and must not have been exhibited at UVA before, must be original to the entering artist, and must not have been made with AI. Two- and three-dimensional work are both accepted, up to 60 inches on the longest side and 40 pounds, with a diptych or triptych measured as a whole; pieces arrive ready to hang with picture wire, since sawtooth hangers and clips are refused, and three-dimensional work needs a sturdy base. Artists may price the work or list it NFS, but a value is required either way for insurance, and UVA passes 70 per cent of any sale to the artist. There is no entry fee. The only requirement is a current UVA membership, which runs $65 a year for an individual and $95 for a family, $45 with a teacher ID and free with a student ID, and whose published benefits include 'Opportunity to hang one work of art at the annual Members' Show'. Applications close October 16 and artwork is dropped off on October 26 between 10am and 5pm, with mailed artwork accepted by arrangement with UVA staff; every participating artist signs an artist contract by that date. The exhibition runs October 30 to December 23 at the arts centre on West Harvard Avenue in Roseburg, opening with a reception on October 30 from 4pm to 7pm. — Deadline: October 16, 2026. Fee: Free (UVA membership required, $65/year individual). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Printmaking NOW! (10 Years Later) · Umpqua Valley Arts
item.description: Ten years after its 2017 national printmaking survey, Umpqua Valley Arts in Roseburg, Oregon revives the exhibition as Printmaking NOW! (10 Years Later), a curated and juried show open to artists across the nation at every career stage. There is no theme — the focus is printmaking techniques and artists who explore ideas and various modes of the medium, with the accepted-media list explicitly open-ended: woodcuts, linocuts, screen printing, monoprinting, lithography, intaglio, gel plates "and more", with artists exploring the limits of printmaking techniques expressly welcome. The binding requirement is that entries must be made using printmaking techniques, methods and mediums, so this is a show for photogravure, photo-screenprint and other photographic print processes rather than for straight photographs — nothing in the prospectus bars photographic processes, and the eligibility text itself names fine art photography prints as eligible in its documentation clause. Work must have been completed in the last three years, not previously shown at UVA, and stay under 60 inches on the longest side. Juror Heather Halpern, an award-winning artist and instructor from Eugene, makes the selections, with UVA framing the choice of a Pacific Northwest curator as lending a regional voice to the show. Awards are $300, $200 and $100 for first through third place. Entry is $30 for up to three works through CaFE, closing September 25 (11:59pm Mountain / 10:59pm Pacific); artists are notified no later than October 30, accepted work arrives by January 4, and the exhibition runs January 8 to March 13, 2027. — Deadline: September 25, 2026. Fee: $30 (up to 3 works). Prize: $300 / $200 / $100.

item.title: In Cahoots Residency — June–December 2027
item.description: One- to three-week residencies at In Cahoots in Petaluma, California — pastoral Sonoma County, close to San Francisco and the Pacific coast — with a focus on artists' books, letterpress, printmaking, writing and collaboration. The studios specifically support printmakers, letterpress printers, book artists and writers and those applications are given priority, but the residency states it does occasionally host artists working in other mediums such as painting, photography and mixed media — a natural fit for photobook makers and photographers working in print. Three to five residents attend at a time, each with a private guest house or summer sleeping cottage, 24-hour access to the shared studios, weekly grocery runs and group field trips; residents cook for themselves. This application round, open August 27 to October 1, 2026, covers residencies taking place June through December 2027. The residency is self-paying — $995 for one week up to $2,500 for three in an individual cottage, with student rates, cheaper May–October sleeping cottages and a 25% discount for collaborators sharing housing — but ten full or partial Fellowships are awarded for this period (twenty per year), designed for artists for whom the experience would otherwise be out of reach financially, with particular welcome for emerging artists with under ten years in the field, recent students, people of colour, career returners and adjunct teachers; fellowship applicants not selected are automatically considered for a paid place. Applicants must be 18 or older with prior experience in art or writing, and visual artists submit 8–10 images, a CV, application questions and three references through CaFE with a $25 fee. Applications are reviewed by a jury team and decisions go out about eight weeks after the deadline. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $25 + $995–$2,500 stay (fellowships available). Prize: 1–3 week residency (10 funded fellowships).

item.title: Cloud Watchers Volume 2 · arigatos press
item.description: arigatos press — a Mexican-Japanese fanzine project by the artists behind @anafrito and @ceethruportals, publishing fanzines, stickers and photo prints — is compiling the second volume of Cloud Watchers, its zine documenting the cloud. The call, published in English, Spanish and Japanese, wants anything to do with clouds: photos, texts, drawings, paintings, collages, even screenshots — 'we mean anything. We want to celebrate the cloud in all its forms.' For the editors clouds are ethereal and ephemeral, invoking a feeling of awe that immediately opens the imagination. There is also a ritual element carried over from last year: Cloud Appreciation Day falls on Friday, September 11, and entrants are invited to upload a photo of clouds taken that day along with what came to them as they looked at the sky. Submissions are open worldwide ('wherever you are') until Monday, September 14, 2026; more than one contribution per person is welcome, with a separate form completed for each. Entry is free through the form embedded on the open-call page, and selected work is published in Volume 2 — Volume One is already out and viewable on the press's site. — Deadline: September 14, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in Volume 2.

item.title: Locals Only 2027 — Wonder · City of San Ramon
item.description: The City of San Ramon's fourth annual Locals Only juried exhibition takes 'Wonder' as its 2027 theme — the things that inspire curiosity, awe, joy, mystery or imagination, from a remarkable moment in nature to an ordinary object transformed, a memory explored or another world imagined. It is open to San Ramon residents only, and genuinely to every generation: six age categories run from kindergarten through 2nd grade up to adults 18+ and seniors 55+, all in all mediums, with both two- and three-dimensional work accepted. Work must be original and created entirely by the entering artist, with no AI-generated work; pieces shown in last year's San Ramon juried exhibits are not eligible. 2D work may not exceed 30 by 40 inches including the frame and 40 pounds, 3D work 18 inches each way and 50 pounds. Up to three entries per artist at $15 each, with a $5 student rate via coupon code StudentHi5. A blind jury that sees no personal information makes the selections and awards, which are gift certificates: $150 for Best in Show overall, then $75, $50 and $25 blue, red and white ribbons in each category. Applications open January 11, 2027 on CaFE at cityofsanramon.info/localsonly and close March 28; selection notifications go out by email April 2, accepted work is hand-delivered April 22–23, and the exhibition runs May 7–26 at the Dougherty Station Community Arts Center, with a public artists' reception on May 7. Sales carry a 20 per cent commission to the city. — Deadline: March 28, 2027. Fee: $15 per entry ($5 for students). Prize: Gift certificates up to $150.

item.title: IMPRINT · Manifest Gallery
item.description: Manifest Gallery establishes IMPRINT as an annual international exhibition of printmaking, launched alongside the new printmaking studio that opened at the Cincinnati non-profit's permanent home in May 2026 and that operates beside its drawing, painting and darkroom photography programmes. The gallery frames the two disciplines together, writing that “like photography, printmaking is a genre of creative work that is underscored by its processes” and calling printmaking an important checkpoint on the road map between the earliest cave markings and the ubiquitous photography in everyone's pocket today. The call is open to artists worldwide, has no size limit beyond what fits through the gallery door and no restriction on when the work was made, and states no predefined expectation for type or style, with submissions ranging from traditional to conceptual or experimental; the media clause reads “open to all traditional and nontraditional genres and media within the expansive bounds of printmaking”. The one hard limit is that printmaking must be the work's primary medium, which makes this a show for photogravure, photopolymer, photo-screenprint and other photographic print processes rather than for straight photographs. Selection runs in two stages: an anonymous multi-member panel of professional and academic advisors juries the entries, then passes its recommendations to the exhibition curator, who makes the final selections from the jury-approved pool. Every exhibiting artist receives a $50 cash honorarium, and one work from this exhibition period wins a $1,000 Grand Jury Award decided by a second-round jury drawn from the top-scoring works; Manifest runs that award in each of the nine exhibition periods of its 23rd season. Selected work is shown December 11, 2026 to January 8, 2027 and documented in the season annual. Entry is $45 for up to three works and $5 for each additional work, with no cap on the number of entries, and artists receive 70% of any sale. — Deadline: September 12, 2026. Fee: $45 (3 images) + $5 each. Prize: $1,000.

item.title: Old, New, Borrowed, Blue · L7 Gallery
item.description: L7 Gallery is an independent contemporary gallery run from Bellingham, Washington by curator Jo Ford (BFA San Francisco Art Institute, MFA UC Berkeley) and Blaise Smith, which presents its juried exhibitions online. For its October 2026 exhibit the gallery invites artists to respond to the four themes in the traditional Victorian rhyme "Something old, something new, something borrowed, something blue" — a familiar wedding poem whose origin, the gallery notes, lay in magical charms used to ward off evil and protect future generations. It asks what those words could possibly mean right now, "in a world of cultural recycling, generative AI, overwhelming tech capital, political and ecological anxiety, loneliness, isolation and the existential fear of the future". OLD is offered as history, tradition, nostalgia, forgotten or rediscovered stories and objects that reappear from the past; NEW as an experiment, a new medium, a new approach or collaboration; BORROWED as found material, borrowed identities, inspirations from channelled entities and ideas drawn from cultural interactions; BLUE as the colour itself, sadness, longing, distance, water, sky, bruises, dreams, loss, hope — whatever blue means to you. Artists may respond to one or all four categories with new or existing work, and the gallery says it is especially interested in work that is personal, strange, uncomfortable, beautiful, experimental, craft or concept oriented (or both), or simply difficult to categorise. Photography is named in the accepted media alongside painting, drawing, watercolour, sculpture, digital art, printmaking and fabric art. Open to artists 18 and over; $30 covers one to three images. The exhibition runs 10 October to 10 November 2026 and is juried by Hannah Sage Kay, an arts writer and critic based between New York and Los Angeles who has contributed to ARTnews, The Art Newspaper, Autre, BOMB, The Brooklyn Rail, the Financial Times, The Guardian, the Los Angeles Review of Books and Nka Journal of Contemporary African Art. One winner receives a $300 cash award and two further artists receive honourable mentions from the juror. All work must be for sale for the run of the show and cannot be withdrawn before it ends; artists receive 60% of the sale price, and prices set at application cannot be changed later. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: $30 (1–3 images). Prize: $300 + Exhibition.

item.title: Shuttles Issue 03 — Destination
item.description: Shuttles is an independent quarterly online exhibition dedicated to migrant creators, which describes itself as an archive of journeys told in images. It values the complexity of migrant memory and lived experience not only as part of individual life histories but as forces that continuously shape social imagination, cultural perception and public narratives, and it exists because so many of the memories formed in crossing countries, institutions and cultural borders remain private, fragmented and unarchived — the aim is "an open, low-threshold online platform where independent work can be seen, encountered, and discussed". Issue 03 takes the theme Destination. The editors write that the word is often very hard for migrants to define, because it marks an end of a journey: "destination is like a ghost haunting us. When we feel lost, we long to set a destination; when we have a clear destination in mind, we are constantly preoccupied with how far we still have to go; and when we finally reach or approach that destination, we cannot help but question whether this is truly what we wanted." The only certain destinations in the journey of migration, they add, are the ones printed on travel tickets. Contributors are asked whether they have a destination, where it is, how far from it they are, or whether they have grown so used to floating that they no longer look for one, and invited to share those experiences and thoughts in still or moving images. Submissions are welcome from anyone who self-identifies as a migrant and is passionate about image-making; both photographic and video work are accepted. Up to five photographs may be sent, but they should belong to a single collection, uploaded as JPEG, PNG, TIFF or PDF, with video and any file over 100MB supplied as a downloadable link instead. The form also asks for the work's title, the equipment and editing software used, the year and location, a short comment on the work and a roughly 50-word introduction to yourself. Alongside the call the editors host an optional online seminar for contributors to discuss each other's work, creative processes and experiences, to be held before the issue is released in mid-October. Free to enter. Three collections have been published so far: Home, On The Road, and a special issue, Our Life in Cisarua. — Deadline: October 2, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Publication in Issue 03.

item.title: 12th DGPh Bildungspreis 2026
item.description: The DGPh Bildungspreis is the German Photographic Society's prize for photographic education, awarded in 2026 for the twelfth time and endowed for the first time with €3,000. The DGPh — a non-profit founded in 1951 — states the prize's purpose as discovering and making known interesting projects in the mediation of and with photography. It is looking for innovative and sustainable projects that use photography as a language and reach into society: cultural and museum-education initiatives in which photography is the subject or the tool, media education offerings about photography, school and out-of-school activities, and innovative projects from universities. The society describes the range of possible submissions as deliberately wide — new mediation concepts in schools, photography projects and workshops on selected current themes, innovative formats for making photography tangible, or the creation of a network for photography — and points to the previous years' winning projects as evidence of that openness to very different approaches. The award is explicitly a Förderpreis, offered to projects still taking shape as well as finished ones, and from 2026 it will be awarded every two years. An application needs a substantial project description; photographs and any existing press coverage may be attached, and the online portal asks for four to fifteen image examples of previous work as JPEGs. Entry is free, and submissions are accepted only through the DGPh's own online portal. The jury is made up of the board of the DGPh's Education Section together with further experts in photography mediation, always including the previous year's laureate; the section is responsible for the design and award of the prize. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,000.

item.title: Light & Shadow · Aurea Photogallery
item.description: Aurea Photogallery's open call on contrast, asking photographers to work with the balance between light and darkness. The gallery is looking for geometric shadows and urban patterns, dramatic chiaroscuro lighting, bold silhouettes and backlit subjects, and the subtler transitions between light and dark — in black and white or in colour. Selected work runs in a one-month online exhibition (24 September – 31 October 2026) with a free PDF catalogue and a print-on-demand edition, a dedicated artist page linking to the photographer's own site, and permanent inclusion in the gallery's archive. Submissions are free and reviewed on a rolling basis with a response within 72 hours; a one-time €30 curation and exhibition fee applies only to photographers whose work is selected. The gallery takes no commission and handles no sales. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: Free (€30 if accepted). Prize: Exhibition + Catalog.

item.title: Prémio NARRATIVA – FUJIFILM 2026
item.description: Second edition of the photography award run by NARRATIVA, a non-profit association and Lisbon photography space, together with Fujifilm Portugal, its main patron. The award is open to all fields of photography and looks for original, unpublished projects that build visual narratives around contemporary issues; the jury weighs the relevance of the theme, the project's impact, conceptual and narrative coherence, and originality. The winner receives €3,500 and a solo exhibition at NARRATIVA in Lisbon, scheduled to open in January 2027, and the jury may name up to two honourable mentions whose projects are publicly presented at NARRATIVA. Applications run from 1 to 30 September 2026 through a form on NARRATIVA's own website and ask for a biography of up to 1,000 characters, a project title, a synopsis of up to 2,000 characters, and 15 to 20 JPEGs (3000px on the long edge, 72dpi, 2MB maximum) renamed 001, 002, 003 in reading order and stripped of the author's name and project title, so the reading is anonymous. Entry is free. Eligibility is narrow: applicants must be 18 or over, resident in Portugal and with tax domicile there, at either an emerging or established stage. Projects made in educational or academic contexts are welcome, but work developed in NARRATIVA's own workshops and masterclass is not, and current or former NARRATIVA members, Fujifilm X-Photographers and Fujifilm employees may not enter. Only basic adjustments to colour, contrast and framing are allowed and AI tools are barred outright. Two conditions are worth reading before entering: the winner must travel to and attend the exhibition opening and an accompanying talk or guided tour, and any honourable mentions must attend the public presentation of their projects on a date still to be set, and under the regulations one work from the exhibition enters NARRATIVA's collection while the remaining prints are stored for a year for possible showings at partner venues and destroyed after that. The jury for this edition is named — Yael Martínez, the Magnum photographer and W. Eugene Smith Grant and two-time World Press Photo winner; Ana Rocha, a designer at the photobook publisher GOST Books; and Mário Cruz, NARRATIVA's founder and director and himself a two-time World Press Photo winner. — Deadline: September 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €3,500 + solo exhibition.

item.title: TARZEER Grant for Photography 2027
item.description: First edition of a grant from Tarzeer Pictures, a Manila gallery and studio whose programme runs exhibitions, projections and a roster of Philippine image-makers. The grant supports the development of a new photographic project for exhibition, and selected recipients receive a total of PHP 300,000: a Project Fund of PHP 200,000 to produce the work during 2027, and an Exhibition Fund of PHP 100,000 to present it in a show at Tarzeer Pictures. The call is open to individuals working across all modes and forms of photography — new or ongoing projects that have not yet been exhibited, presented as still images, multimedia or mixed media. Applicants must be Filipino and 18 or over, at any stage of their career; students may apply as long as the project is not a school requirement, and Filipinos living abroad may apply and may make the work wherever they propose, with no requirement to produce it in the Philippines. One entry per applicant, and applying is free. The application portal opens 1 September 2026 and closes 15 October 2026 at 11:59pm Philippine Standard Time; everything goes in as a single PDF of 25MB or less containing a 150-word biography, a project proposal (cover, a 100–200 word project statement, a 250–500 word artist statement), up to fifteen pages of work samples, and a two-table funding plan itemising how the Project and Exhibition Funds would be spent. There are no restrictions on how the money is spent as long as it can be justified. Shortlisted applicants are invited to present their projects to the Selection Committee — Tarzeer Pictures plus a special jury — during November 2026, and recipients are announced in January 2027; the number of grantees is decided during selection. Images made with AI or machine learning are barred in any capacity. Recipients keep copyright, but grant Tarzeer exclusive rights of first exhibition within a year of the project's completion, including the sale of exhibited works on agreed terms, with the gallery's commission going back into funding future grants, plus non-exclusive non-commercial use for publicity and catalogues. The grant is framed as a partnership: recipients give regular production updates and take part in the gallery's public programmes during the exhibition. — Deadline: October 15, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: PHP 300,000 + exhibition.

item.title: Prairie Ronde Artist Residency — Spring 2027
item.description: Spring session of the residency at The Mill at Vicksburg, a former Lee Paper Company mill on eighty acres in the village of Vicksburg, Michigan, now a redevelopment project. The Spring 2027 session runs March 15 to May 31, with two to four residents in residence for five to six weeks. The programme does not limit the residency to any specific medium, so photographers are eligible alongside every other discipline; what it looks for is independent, engaged and curious artists who can creatively interact with The Mill and its surrounding property. Residents receive a $2,000 stipend on completion, a $500 travel grant, private housing, a gallery show in downtown Vicksburg, video documentation of their time there and a membership to the Mug Club at the Distant Whistle Brewery. In return, Prairie Ronde is process-based rather than product-based, and asks that each artist donate one piece made during the residency to its permanent collection. Applications open on September 1, 2026 and are due December 1, 2026, with selections announced January 15, 2027; there is a $25 application fee, which the organisers say covers SlideRoom costs and an honorarium for the review panellists. Applications are scored against a published rubric — the body of work, the statement of purpose, the plan for incorporating The Mill or Vicksburg, evidence of genuine research into the programme, the ability to thrive independently, and openness to living in a rural community — and the highest-scoring applicants are then interviewed by the Residency Director and Coordinator. One restriction to note before applying: since April 25, 2025 the programme has temporarily suspended its consideration of international applicants, so it is effectively open to US-based artists for now. Note also that the page states the stipend as $2,000 in its list of what the residency offers but refers to a $2,500 stipend in its answer about collaborative applications; the lower published figure is the one recorded here. — Deadline: December 1, 2026. Fee: $25. Prize: $2,000 stipend + $500 travel grant + housing + gallery show.

item.title: THE REVEAL: The Sublime Uncertainty of Almost Knowing · ShadowBoxX Gallery
item.description: Inaugural international print biennial from ShadowBoxX Gallery in downtown Waukegan, Illinois, co-sponsored by the Waukegan Printmakers Association. The theme is the moment every printmaker knows: the work is done, the decisions are made, the outcome has been imagined, and still, for one brief moment, you almost know. Entries must be original work that substantially uses an analog printmaking process, and the organisers' list of eligible processes runs from etching, engraving, drypoint, aquatint and mezzotint through linocut, woodcut, wood engraving, stone and plate lithography, monotype, monoprint, collagraph and traditional screenprinting to cyanotype and “related historic, alternative and experimental analog printmaking processes” — which is the way in for photographers working in cyanotype and other alternative processes. Mixed-media and hybrid works qualify when an analog printmaking process is a substantial and identifiable component of the finished piece. Digital technology used incidentally during development does not automatically disqualify a work, but digital printing may not be the primary means by which the finished image is produced, and giclée prints, inkjet reproductions, commercial digital reproductions, photographic reproductions of paintings or drawings and AI-generated imagery reproduced as prints are all ineligible. There is no size limit; editioned prints, variable editions, monoprints, monotypes and other unique impressions are all accepted. Selected work is exhibited for roughly three months, opening in conjunction with November ArtWauk and running from November 2026 into February 2027, with a collectors' preview on Zoom before the reception. Sales are split 50/50 with the gallery and artists set their own prices; artists cover shipping and, for international entrants, customs. THE REVEAL is conceived as a recurring biennial and returns in 2028. One caution: the organiser publishes two different closing dates — the CaFÉ portal that takes the entries is set to close 1 October 2026, while the prospectus text gives 24 October twice, in the call summary and in the legal agreement's list of important dates. The earlier, portal-enforced date is the one stored here. — Deadline: October 1, 2026. Fee: $20, $5 each additional image. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: 2026 Small Works Juried Exhibition · Five Points Arts
item.description: An international juried small-works show at Five Points Gallery, the exhibition arm of Five Points Arts — a 501(c)(3) that describes itself as one of Connecticut's largest and most respected arts non-profits. Open to all artists 18 or older working in any style or medium, with a single size rule: no dimension may exceed 24 inches, frame included. Up to three works per artist for a flat $35 CaFÉ fee. Only work that has not previously been exhibited at Five Points Gallery is considered. The one award is a solo exhibition in Five Points Gallery in 2027/28, announced at 7 pm during the opening reception. Juror is Patricia Carrigan, a Connecticut painter and mixed media artist who has exhibited nationally and internationally since 1990 and has taught visual fine arts at Manchester Community College for over twenty years. Submissions open September 1, 2026 and close October 11 at 11:59 pm; jurying runs October 13–23, notification is October 25 on CaFÉ, and accepted work is delivered between October 27 and November 13. The exhibition runs November 20, 2026 to January 9, 2027 at 7 Water Street, Torrington, with the opening reception on November 20, 6–8 pm. All work must be for sale and the gallery retains a 50% commission; accepted pieces are also shown on the Five Points website. — Deadline: October 11, 2026. Fee: $35 for up to 3 works. Prize: Solo exhibition.

item.title: Wytches II · Dorado 806 Projects
item.description: A group show at Dorado 806 Projects, an artist-run studio gallery on Broadway in Santa Monica, built around the witch as a figure of intuition and connection to the earth rather than the patriarchal caricature. The curators describe digging into 'the enchantment of moonlight and the rhythms of nature to look at the intuitive, connected beings who have been unjustly stigmatized throughout history'. Photography is named outright among the accepted media, alongside painting, drawing, printmaking, fiber and sculpture. Work must be original, unsold, wholly the artist's copyright, and no more than 36 inches in any direction — though a series of individually compliant pieces may be submitted together. Works on paper must be framed and everything arrives ready to hang. $35 covers up to three images. Curated by Amelie Laurice and Meghan DeRoma; the opening reception is October 7, 2026, with an in-person run of about four weeks and an online show to November 30. Sales split 50/50, with Dorado donating a portion of its share to a local non-profit, and the gallery states that entry fees fund its free community events and group exhibitions. Artists are responsible for delivery and collection. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $35 for up to 3 images. Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: Artistic Innovations Grants for Individual Artists FY2027 · Mid-America Arts Alliance
item.description: Grants of up to $15,000 for individual artists to make and present new, original work — and, as of the August 2026 cycle, with no cost share or match required, a change funded by Mid-America Arts Alliance's reinvestment of a gift from Yield Giving. Photography is listed as a discipline in its own right in the eligibility guidelines, separate from the Visual Arts category. Applicants must be at least 21, be a US citizen, permanent resident or hold non-resident status, and be a full-time resident of the six-state M-AAA region — Arkansas, Kansas, Missouri, Nebraska, Oklahoma, Texas, and the Native Nations in this geography — both before the deadline and throughout the grant period. Projects must introduce a new original idea or artwork at any stage of development and include at least two public-facing engagements in the region between January 1 and June 30, 2027: a feature or premiere presentation of at least 60 minutes, and an outreach or educational activity of at least 30 minutes with direct artist-audience interaction. Applications are adjudicated October 1 to November 30 by a panel of arts professionals scoring against criteria adapted from the National Endowment for the Arts' Artistic Merit and Artistic Excellence rubrics. M-AAA intends to award at least one individual artist grant per state, with no fewer than 18 grantees in the FY2027 cycle. Applicants new to M-AAA are explicitly encouraged, as are artists serving underserved communities. The deadline is 5:00 pm CT on September 24, 2026; selections are notified December 18, 2026 and announced publicly in January 2027. — Deadline: September 24, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: Up to $15,000.

item.title: Oddly Familiar — 2026 Members Exhibition · East Bay Photo Collective
item.description: EBPCO's annual members' show, on the déjà-vu sensation of liminal space — 'places that look exactly like memories from your childhood, but you can't quite place where or when you saw them'. The brief asks for the unexpected angle rather than the grand view: the organisers frame it as 'less Ansel Adams and more Edward Weston. Less Martin Scorsese, more Quentin Tarantino. Less Steven Spielberg, more Wes Anderson.' Work must be photography-based — traditional, digital or alternative process — made in the last three to five years, not previously exhibited at Oakland Photo Workshop, and not made with generative AI. Framed dimensions cannot exceed 24 inches and accepted work arrives framed and ready to hang. Members may submit up to five images at no charge, and membership is open to anyone at $50 a year, $250 premium, or $25 for students and low-income artists; it must be active through December 4, 2026. Jurying is blind, by Kendra Luck and Kevin Flynn, and the collective typically accepts 30–50 pieces for the gallery plus another 10–20 for the online exhibition, with a catalogue for sale after opening. Submissions close September 28 at 11:59 pm PT, notification is October 11, artwork drop-off is mid-November, and the exhibition runs December 4 to January 17 at Oakland Photo Workshop, opening Friday December 4, 6–9 pm. A virtual office-hours session for submission help runs September 15. — Deadline: September 28, 2026. Fee: Free (EBPCO membership required, from $25/year). Prize: Exhibition.

item.title: David Whitehouse Research Residency for Artists · Corning Museum of Glass
item.description: A funded research residency at one of the world's great glass collections, for artists who want to work in an archive rather than a hot shop. The David Whitehouse Research Residency gives artists dedicated time with the holdings of the Rakow Research Library and the Museum's permanent collection, with support from expert Museum and Library staff. It is explicitly not a glassmaking residency and no provision is made for creating work at The Studio. Residencies run one, two or three weeks and can be scheduled at any point in the following year, with applicants prioritising their own availability on the form. Transportation, room and board are provided, and a residency manager acts as liaison in Corning and at the Museum. Recipients are invited to give a free public lecture at The Studio about their practice or research. Applications go through SlideRoom and need a written proposal of the research plan, 10 digital images of your work, a résumé, an artist statement and two letters of recommendation. Selected applicants are notified in November and the full list of residents is announced each January. The call names no media, but the Museum's published roster of past residents settles it: alongside glassblowers, ceramicists and sculptors it includes Phoebe Stubbs, whose video installations and photographic experiments treat glass as the membrane through which every photographic image is mediated, using blown objects as lenses and diffusers. Past residents have come from Australia, Turkey, Mexico, England and New Zealand. — Deadline: August 31, 2026. Fee: $30. Prize: Funded residency (travel, room and board).

item.title: In Contrast 2026 · Maryland Federation of Art
item.description: Maryland Federation of Art's juried group show on contrast as a working tool — the chiaroscuro of the Baroque and the oppositions of Fauvist colour, but equally contrasts of texture, subject and concept. Selected work is shown in MFA's Virtual Gallery from 15 December 2026 to 14 February 2027. All MFA exhibitions are blind juried, with artists' names and identifying information hidden from the juror; this edition is selected by Sena Clara Creston, an interactive installation artist and Associate Professor of Media Arts at Sonoma State University, who studied Photography and Imaging at NYU and took an MFA in Electronic Arts from RPI. Cash awards presented by the juror total $500, announced 7 January 2027. Artists working in all mediums are invited and any original 2D or 3D work is considered; up to 6 original works made in the past three years may be entered, and work previously exhibited in MFA's Virtual Gallery is not eligible for re-entry. Because this is an online show, MFA's General Guidelines open it to artists worldwide with the exception of sanctioned countries — the call page also carries a US/Canada/Mexico line copied from the physical Circle Gallery shows, which the guidelines and the entry form both override. Only artists in the 48 contiguous United States may set a sale price, and MFA reimburses up to $35 of their shipping on online sales; everyone else lists Price on Request and MFA refers enquiries to them. Artists are notified 19 November and retain 80% of sales (85% for members). Founded in 1963, MFA is a non-profit whose Circle Gallery in Annapolis is Maryland's oldest operating artist gallery. — Deadline: October 21, 2026. Fee: $45/2 works ($30 members) + $6.75 each addl. Prize: $500 + exhibition.

item.title: Photography Commission: National Folklore Collection · UCD Library
item.description: A €20,000 photographic commission from UCD Library, marking the move of Ireland's National Folklore Collection out of the Newman Building — its home since 1971 — and into the new Cultural Heritage Centre inside the James Joyce Library. The NFC is internationally recognised as one of Europe's most important ethnographic archives, and its Irish Folklore Commission Collection (1935–1970) has been inscribed on UNESCO's Memory of the World Register since 2017. One photographer or lens-based artist will make an original series of 15 to 25 works responding to the transition, with facilitated access to the archive spaces, the reading room, selected collection material, and the librarians, archivists, researchers and conservators who work there.
