The brief is deliberately open to documentary, conceptual, research-led and contemporary approaches, and suggests themes from archives and memory to conservation, institutional architecture, and the relationship between place and memory; the panel asks for proposals that are evocative, optimistic, dynamic, democratic and human-centred, framing the relocation as renewal rather than an ending. A selection of the finished work goes into a public exhibition, anticipated for May 2027, with printing, framing and installation commissioned separately by the Library. Copyright stays with the artist, who grants UCD Library a perpetual, non-exclusive, royalty-free licence to exhibit, publish and archive the work; commercial licensing needs a separate agreement. At least 25% of the proposed budget must be allocated to the artist's fee, and the commission is paid in four quarters against contract, research, draft and final delivery. Applications are a single PDF of up to 20MB — CV, artist statement, a 500-word commission proposal, a 500-word research methodology, an indicative timeline, an itemised budget and five portfolio images — emailed by 12 noon. Site visits run 31 August and 1 September, bookable by email, and the deadline for queries is 4 September. UCD Library says it particularly welcomes applications from artists underrepresented in the arts and cultural sector, and offers accessibility supports and alternative submission formats on request. — Deadline: September 16, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: €20,000 commission + exhibition.

item.title: Ballarat Youth Photography Prize 2026 · Ballarat International Foto Biennale
item.description: Developed by GroupFoto, the Ballarat International Foto Biennale's youth council, this free prize is open to young photographic artists aged 12 to 25 who live, work or study in Ballarat or Victoria's Central Highlands — the municipalities of Ararat Rural City, City of Ballarat, Golden Plains Shire, Hepburn Shire, Moorabool Shire and Pyrenees Shire. There are two categories. Open takes photographs of any subject, idea, person, place or moment, with no set theme. The themed category, Connected, invites photographs exploring the many ways we experience connection — relationships with Country, family, friends, culture, identity, community, place or animals, or how technology shapes connection through phones, gaming, social media, online communities, surveillance or access. Each category may be entered once, with a single photograph; series are not accepted. The Biennale says you do not need professional equipment or previous photography experience to be considered, and phone photographs are accepted (upload the highest-quality version you have). Every eligible entry will be printed and included in the exhibition at the National Centre for Photography, running 20 September to 4 October 2026. Five cash prizes of at least $150 each are presented: a winner in each category for each age group (12–17 and 18–25), plus the UFS People's Choice Award, voted during the exhibition and announced on 6 October. Judging is by Ballarat International Foto Biennale staff and members of GroupFoto; GroupFoto participants may enter and have eligible work exhibited but are not eligible to receive a prize. Entrants under 18 need a parent or guardian's consent, and images created using generative AI are not eligible. — Deadline: August 30, 2026. Fee: Free. Prize: 5 × A$150 minimum + Exhibition.

item.title: ELEVEN: Be There · Viewpoint Photographic Art Center
item.description: ELEVEN is Viewpoint Photographic Art Center's end-of-year juried exhibition, and one of four group open calls the Sacramento non-profit runs annually — the November/December themed slot, which the centre states is open to all and does not require membership. The 2026 theme is Be There, taken from the reply Weegee is said to have given when asked the secret of his success: "F8 and be there." Viewpoint is after photographs that came out of preparation, seeking, opportunity and actually being present, whether that is a child's first step, light thrown by a skyscraper's windows, or the quietude implied by new snow. Juror Jeff Redman founded and ran Lightwork, a photographers' supply shop and gallery in Sacramento, from 1980 to 1997, curating exhibits there for Linda McCartney, Ruth Bernhard, Roy DeCarava and Morley Baer among dozens of others; he went on to found Viewpoint itself in 1991 with the support of other charter members, and learned carbon printing during Covid. Awards are $333 for first place, $222 for second, $111 for third and $111 for Curator's Choice, plus two honourable mentions of a Viewpoint workshop valued at $95. Up to six images may be entered, and a multiple-image set such as a diptych or triptych counts as one image and is submitted as a single file. Judging is anonymous, so files must not be signed, watermarked or named after the entrant. Each entry also has to declare the print's photographic medium (inkjet, gelatin silver, alt process, metal or other), image size, mat size and price. Accepted prints are delivered between September 30 and October 24; overall size including mat may not exceed 18 by 24 inches, or 20 by 20 for square images. The exhibit runs November 11 to December 19 2026 at the gallery on J Street, with a second-Sunday reception on November 15, and the online exhibit continues to January 20 2027. Prints offered for sale need a minimum price of $80, and Viewpoint splits sales 50/50 with the artist. — Deadline: September 19, 2026. Fee: $22 (1 image), $33 (2–3 images), $44 (4–6 images). Prize: $333 first, $222 second, $111 third, $111 Curator's Choice.

item.title: 13th Annual Small Works Exhibition 2026 · Main Street Arts
item.description: Main Street Arts is a non-profit gallery in the village of Clifton Springs, New York, occupying a 3,600-square-foot building over two floors with exhibitions, workshops, youth programs and an art resource library. Its Small Works show is the thirteenth annual national juried exhibition of work measuring 12 inches or less per side; framing may extend the whole piece to 16 inches total, but the artwork itself has to stay within 12. The call is open to artists working in all media excluding video/sound and installation art, and to all U.S. residents 18 years or older. $2,000 in cash awards is split between a $1,000 Best in Show, two Main Street Arts Choice Awards of $250 each and ten honourable mentions of $50. Entry is $30 to apply with one, two or three pieces. The juror for this edition has not been named yet — the 2025 show was juried by gallery curator Heather Olson. Selection is made from the images submitted through Submittable, so nothing should be sent until an acceptance email arrives; JPEGs should be at least 1000 pixels in any direction and named after the artwork. Accepted work is due by October 10 and may be delivered in person or shipped by UPS with a pre-paid return label valid for 90 days. The exhibition fills the main-floor gallery and runs online alongside it from November 7 to December 23 2026, opening with an artist reception on the afternoon of November 7. — Deadline: September 20, 2026. Fee: $30 (1–3 works). Prize: $2,000 in cash awards ($1,000 Best in Show).

item.title: 2026 Bay Area Open · GearBox Gallery
item.description: GearBox Gallery is an artist-run space on West Grand Avenue in Oakland, and the Bay Area Open is its call for a two-person featured exhibition in the Main Gallery. Two artists are chosen to show together from November 5 to December 19 2026, with an opening reception on Saturday November 7. Entry is open to artists living in the nine Greater Bay Area counties — Alameda, Contra Costa, Marin, Napa, San Francisco, San Mateo, Santa Clara, Solano and Sonoma — who have a current, cohesive body of work made within the last five years. Applicants submit 8 to 12 images along with an artist statement about the work rather than about wanting to show at GearBox, and the gallery says image quality will be an important factor in jurying. There are no media or size limitations. The curatorial team selects which of the submitted pieces to hang, so not everything entered is necessarily shown; the aim is to present a substantial body of work from each of the two artists. The processing fee is $35 per application rather than per image. Notification goes out by email on September 28 2026, and accepted work is delivered in person on November 1 or the morning of November 2 — the gallery does not accept mailed work. Submitted artwork must be for sale, and GearBox pays the artist 60% of the sale price within 30 days of the exhibition closing. Pick-up is scheduled between December 20 2026 and January 3 2027. Entries go through CaFE at callforentry.org, where the 2026 Bay Area Open listing is now live. — Deadline: September 21, 2026. Fee: $35. Prize: Two-person featured exhibition.

item.title: Autumn Juried Show 2026 · Rowayton Arts Center
item.description: Rowayton Arts Center is a non-profit gallery on Rowayton Avenue in Norwalk, Connecticut, and its Autumn Juried Show is an open-call, open-theme, all-media exhibition. Photography is named outright in the accepted-media list in both colour and black and white, and the centre's blanket ban on giclee reproductions is explicitly waived for photography and digital art. The juror is Kimberly Henrikson, executive director of the Center for Contemporary Printmaking, a non-profit print organisation that has run for over thirty years in Norwalk with a regular exhibition schedule, instructional workshops, an artist-in-residence programme, studio rental space and edition printing for artists. There is a $250 cash award for Best in Show. Entry is $35 for a first piece and $10 for each additional piece up to five for non-members, $25 and $10 for members, and $2 and $1 for the centre's Art Angel life members; a maximum of two pieces per artist can be juried into the show. Work must have been created in the last three years and not previously exhibited at RAC, must be two-dimensional and no more than 40 inches in height or length including the frame, and must be ready to hang on braided wire — no sawtooth hangers. Artwork generated by AI is not acceptable. Accepted pieces have to be hand delivered on October 12 or 13; the centre will not accept work that is mailed in, which in practice limits this to artists who can get to Norwalk. The show runs October 18 to November 14 2026 with an opening reception on the afternoon of October 18, and RAC takes a 30% commission on sales. — Deadline: September 11, 2026. Fee: $35 first piece + $10 each additional ($25 + $10 members). Prize: $250 Best in Show.
